pageCache.pageTitle: Private School in Buckinghamshire - Akeley Wood School
pageCache.text:
An adventure for today An education for tomorrow
School, education, childhood is not just a journey to an imagined and hoped for future. It is an adventure your child is living right now. It happens so fast, it’s over so quickly, it matters so much. That’s why it’s our job as educators to make school, education, childhood, an inspiring, enriching and rewarding experience - right when it is actually happening. Not just a set of key stages to grind through to a hoped for end. At Akeley Wood School, we help your child discover their talents and interests. Help them grow their character. Develop courage and responsibility. And discover their place in the world.
In an inspiring, nurturing, open and inquisitive environment...
...with the very best facilities, diverse curriculum and supportive teachers. We set your child up to achieve their very best, both personally and academically. To go on out there into the wider world as an interested and interesting person. With the skills, knowledge and results they need to fulfil their dreams. Drawing on a childhood full of joy, curiosity and adventure. Because a wondrous childhood makes for a wonderful life. We believe your child’s today matters as much as their tomorrow. So at Akeley Wood we make education an adventure. Something remarkable, memorable and valuable forever. We shape the interested and interesting people the world needs. Universities, employers - society as a whole – needs curious, independent thinkers, full of courage and responsibility. Our aim is to shape these people.
Location and Facilities
Explore our idyllic campuses
Akeley Wood School is a vibrant, co-educational day school for children aged 1 to 18, set across two beautiful campuses in Buckinghamshire and Northamptonshire. Both sites are inspirational learning environments for our students at different stages, from early curiosity to senior academic readiness and sixth form independence. This thoughtful design and our commitment to personalised learning ensure that students at Akeley Wood thrive, both academically and socially, in a nurturing and supportive environment.
Begin your Akeley Wood School journey.
Straightforward and simple
Discover. Grow. Achieve. At Akeley Wood.
Follow Akeley Wood on Social Media
- Welcome Back -We threw our doors open again to our pupils today, ready for a brand new school year full of opportunities. A very warm welcome to all of our returning families and those joining us for the very first time too! We are delighted to have you with us.
- Active Participants - As we get ready to welcome our students back and our Sixth Formers into their fully refurbished AW6, we just HAD to share some more BTS shots with you of this beautiful space. Just the last finishing touches to go! We cannot wait for you to see it for yourselves and to make it your own. Happy Bank Holiday weekend everyone! 💚
Not long now!In 1 week we welcome back our students for a brand new school year and we can’t wait!
- GCSE Highlights - Just a few highlights from yesterday’s results day. Wishing all of our students and their families a weekend of celebrations. 👏
- GCSE Results Day 2026 - “Today was a day of real celebration for our pupils as the culmination of their hard work was rewarded with some wonderful and well deserved grades. The support that our pupils have received from their teachers has been invaluable and, of course, we know that without the support of parents and carers our children would not have performed as well as they have.“It has been lovely to meet more of the Akeley Wood community today and we look forward to welcoming our pupils back to school in a couple of weeks when they begin their Sixth Form journeys at AW6.”Mr Jonathan Stevens, Head of Seniors
BTS at AW6 this summer. 👀The team are busy getting our newly refurbished Sixth Form ready for September. We can’t wait to see the finished product and to share it with our students.
- Academic Excellence -As GCSE Results Day approaches, we would like to wish all of our Year 11 students the very best of luck. 🍀Thursday marks the culmination of years of hard work, commitment and perseverance, and we are incredibly proud of everything our students have achieved along the way.We look forward to celebrating alongside you and your families and supporting you as you take your next steps. Good luck, Year 11!If you are a student who receives their results this week and would like to discover more about Akeley Wood Sixth Form, our Admissions Manager, Senior Leaders and Careers & Futures Lead, Ms Batchelor will remain in place for you to talk to about what Akeley Wood could offer for your A Level journey. Come in and speak with us after you have collected your results.
- Introducing Mr Jonathan Stevens - We are delighted to announce the appointment of Jonathan Stevens as the new Headteacher of Akeley Wood Seniors. Jonathan joins Akeley Wood from Cokethorpe School, where he has served as Deputy Head since 2013. He brings with him a wealth of experience spanning both pastoral care and academic leadership, underpinned by a deep commitment to nurturing the potential of every pupil. Prior to his time at Cokethorpe, Jonathan was a boarding Housemaster and mathematics teacher at Eastbourne College. He began his teaching career in Zimbabwe, an experience that helped shape his inclusive outlook and passion for educational excellence. Jonathan’s breadth of experience, combined with his strong leadership and dedication to holistic education, make him exceptionally well placed to lead Akeley Wood School into its next chapter. Jonathan said:“I am truly excited and honoured to be joining the Akeley Wood community. From my first interactions, it was clear that this is a school with a strong sense of purpose and a warm, ambitious spirit. I very much look forward to getting to know the pupils, staff and families and to working together to build on the school’s many strengths and successes.”
Next Steps
Akeley Wood School

pageCache.pageTitle: Creative & Performing Arts - Senior School - Akeley Wood
pageCache.text:
Creative and Performing Arts
Creative and Performing Arts at Akeley Wood thrives in an environment where self-expression is nurtured, and students collaborate on creative journeys in disciplines including Art, Music, Performance or Textiles. With the ability to specialise and focus on specific areas of interest within each individual discipline, such as photography, music technology and textile art, students are able to fine tune their own individual talents and passions, with the help of a dedicated team of teachers and fantastic facilities.
Art
Music
Performing Arts
Art.
The Art Department sets out to develop our students’ passion for thinking imaginatively and realising their ideas through creation. We pride ourselves in providing a learning environment which fosters problem solving, risk taking, self-expression and ‘happy accidents’. Through our carefully designed schemes of work that allow students to succeed and develop confidence in their skills, they are introduced to experimental mark making, printing and clay work. The experience becomes more tailored to each student as they progress through GCSE and A level when students will create their own projects and the Art teachers, who between them have a wide range of skills, facilitate and support their work.
Inspiring trips.
To inspire and acknowledge Art in our society, we invite practising artists to run workshops on a variety of themes at school. Regular museum and gallery trips to London, Oxford and Birmingham consolidate in-school projects and underline the living, breathing nature of Art and its relevance outside the curriculum. Students typically visit Kew Gardens and nearby Compton Verney during their GCSE course.
Competitions.
In recent years we have submitted our students’ work to local and national competitions where we have had great success, and in 2021 we were shortlisted for Innovation and Excellence in Fine Arts by the ISA. We round off the school year with a great celebration of the students’ creations in a big summer exhibition. We aim to give everyone the skills to express themselves creatively.
Inclusivity is at the core of our Music programme at Akeley, whether it be in the classroom, during our extra-curricular activities or through our extensive instrumental and voice tuition programme. We place value in the way in which Music educates, inspires and allows our students to enjoy and flourish. Our curriculum gives students the opportunity to perform, compose and listen to music working collaboratively together and independently as we harness the benefits of music to create well-rounded and confident individuals.
Music facilities.
The Music Department has fully equipped facilities for teaching, rehearsing and performing in, made up of a range of spaces to accommodate students specialising in traditional music as well as music technology. Students benefit from collaborative and individual music practice rooms as well as a music technology studio and mac computers offering industry standard music production software, along with modern recording studio facilities and smaller music practice rooms for peripatetic lessons. We have a programme of performance opportunities throughout the year for students to share their musical talents with the wider school community. We focus on more traditional pieces for the Carol Service, and the Musician of the Year competition inspires our solo star performers. For rock and pop lovers, our musical year culminates in our much-loved festival Akeley Woodfest, showcasing our many school bands and ending the year with a bang. There is something for everyone here.
Performance arts.
The Drama Department is a vibrant and popular place, sitting right at the heart of the school. Drama is taught in all years and offers a place for pupils to explore, experience and examine emotions and feelings, through work studied and devised within the safe boundaries of the classroom and Drama Studio. Our curriculum is designed to help pupils prepare for life, examining intellectual, physical, social and emotional issues through role-play, text and improvisation. Students receive a vocational education with many transferable skills for future careers in theatre and beyond. The Drama Department aims to be a unifying force within the school, motivating pupils of different age groups via public performance.
The Senior School Musical & The Summer Showcase
Drama extends into co-curricular clubs and the annual Senior School Musical, open to all years and one of the much-anticipated school events where the Drama and Music Departments come together. Recent performances have included Chicago and Bugsy Malone. The Summer Showcase provides the GCSE and A level pupils with a very important opportunity to perform their exam work to their parents, friends and teachers. We regularly visit local theatres to watch a variety of performances and take a residential trip to London to watch the most highly acclaimed shows.
Drama programme of study.
During lessons pupils in Years 7-9 follow a lively programme of study which includes diverse theatre genres, scripts from differing time periods and a solid grounding in performance techniques. At GCSE we study the AQA Drama specification, and at A level we study the AQA Theatre Studies specification. We also offer sessions to prepare for LAMDA.
Specialist facilities.
We offer specialisms in Fine Art, Photography and Textiles with excellent facilities. Our photography studio is equipped with the latest Photoshop editing software and we have offer a large range of textiles equipment such as sewing machines, felt-making tools and looms. We have recently finished a major refurbishment of Creative Art facilities at our AW6 Sixth Form campus, where students now benefit from a new Fine Art, Photography and Textiles Studio.
Next Steps
Akeley Wood School

pageCache.pageTitle: Senior School GCSE Results - Akeley Wood, Buckinghamshire
pageCache.text:
GCSE Results
As advocates of a fully-rounded education, our Key stage 4 students are encouraged to keep the range of subjects they choose at GCSE level as wide as possible, ensuring studies are balanced both in terms of knowledge acquisition and learning experiences. We encourage our students to play to their strengths and to be themselves. Brilliantly. In doing so, our Year 11s consistently attain excellent results at GCSE level. Find an in-depth breakdown of our most recent GCSE results below.
GCSE Results
Key Achievements
Akeley Wood Students Celebrate GCSE Success
This year's outcomes highlight the hard work, determination and commitment students have demonstrated throughout their time at the school. Particular highlights include: - 71% of grades were either higher than expectations or met them. - 100% grades 6-9 in Art of which 80% were grades 9-7 - 82% of Biology grades were 9-6 - 67% of Physics grades were 9-6 - 60% of Spanish grades were 8/9 grades - 100% of French grades were 9-5
While all students should be congratulated for their achievements, some individuals accomplished particularly exceptional results, including: · Matvii K - 3 grade 9's; 3 grade 8's; 2 grade 7's · Sam W - 1 grade 9; 6 grades 8's; 1 grade 7; 2 grade 6's · Gabriella A-N all grades achieved 7+
Proud faculty
Head of Senior School, Jonathan Stevens, commented: “Today was a day of real celebration for our pupils as the culmination of their hard work was rewarded with some wonderful and well deserved grades. The support that our pupils have received from their teachers has been invaluable and, of course, we know that without the support of parents and carers our children would not have performed as well as they have. It has been lovely to meet more of the Akeley Wood community today and we look forward to welcoming our pupils back to school in a couple of weeks when they begin their Sixth Form journeys at AW6.”
Next Steps
Akeley Wood School

pageCache.pageTitle: Senior Sports & Competition - Akeley Wood, Buckinghamshire
pageCache.text:
Sports & Competition
A reputation for sporting excellence.
Sport has always played a big part in the day-to-day at Akeley Wood. We have a vision of participation, performance and engagement that we hope to bring to life for each student. We aim to inspire, support and nurture students to fulfil their best in whatever activities they choose, be it academic, sporting or extra-curricular opportunities. We aim to make sure all students can enjoy sports and feel the benefits of physical activity at whatever level they become involved, with several hour hours of outdoor physical education, which includes PE lessons, games and Outdoor Learning timetabled into each week. We work hard to make sure we meet the needs of individuals in these sessions. Whether a student is aiming to hone their skills at county or national level, or simply playing for enjoyment, camaraderie and the associated health benefits, everyone is welcome and valued.
A competitive spirit.
In competition, we have a busy and varied fixture list across the year in the local district schools league, attending and hosting ISA sports events and we perform strongly in National Schools’ Competitions. We have had recent successes at a national level with our teams in cricket, triathlon and athletics, and one of our students is currently representing Scottish Hockey at U18 level. Our team of Sports Staff is led by our Director of Sport, Mr Ben Rolfe. Mr Rolfe and his committed team deliver a broad and varied range of sports and activities, and Sixth Form Sports Leaders support with team management and umpiring at home matches and festivals.
A sports club to appeal to everyone.
After-school sports clubs are available most days for those students wishing to take their game to the next level, with a focus on gameplay, skills and tactical advancement in mainstream sports as well as other gameplay such as basketball, volleyball and girls’ football. We support students competing in sports such as equestrian, triathlon and swimming both in and outside of school, celebrating their successes whenever we can, including in school newsletters, assemblies and at our annual Sports Awards ceremony. Historically our links with local sports clubs are strong, such as Northampton Saints, Stony Stratford and Bucks Cricket. Our students benefit from their coaching and player pathways, and they often use the excellent facilities we have at school.

Senior School Curriculum
An Inspiring Curriculum for GCSEs.
Continuing the holistic approach to whole-child education which we take right through Nursery and Junior School, the rich and varied curriculum at Akeley Wood Senior School is designed to get the very best out of every student, allowing them the space and support in which to discover and nurture their individual strengths and passions. We celebrate the diversity and widespread talents of our students and recognise that they will go on to follow vastly different careers, from city highflyers to sculptors, architects and authors.
GCSE
By teaching an inspiring array of subjects across the curriculum, we give students in Years 7, 8 and 9 the opportunity to build a solid educational foundation, allowing them to make informed choices when they select their GCSE subjects at Key Stage 4. Students are introduced to our Careers and Futures lead, based at the Sixth Form Campus, at this stage. We offer the traditional subjects alongside courses such as Film Studies, Food and Nutrition and Music Technology. Our aim is to be able to inspire all our students. Alongside their academic studies, we encourage students to try something new as part of our Enrichment Curriculum Programme to broaden their horizons.

pageCache.pageTitle: Extra Curricular Activities & Clubs - Akeley Wood Senior School
pageCache.text:
Senior School Extra Curricular Activities
Enhancing the curriculum.
We believe in educating the whole child and offering as many opportunities as possible to learn in different environments and in different ways. Lunchtimes and after school are when many of our weekly clubs take place and as well as sports clubs and musical groups, we have clubs such as Chess, French film club, Verbal Fight Club, The LGBTQ+ Society and Miss Hodgson’s Cooking club – always popular! Students also enjoy our distinct Enriched Curriculum programme, in addition to the fantastic extra-curricular offer at Akeley.
This lively Wednesday lunchtime gathering is for any student who plays an instrument. A wide variety of genres will be explored and music will cater for all performance abilities, from beginners to advanced players. Come along and find out how we can all join together to make some brilliant sounds!
No need to be a grandmaster to enjoy this club - come and test your skills on a Monday lunchtime and learn to play one of the world’s oldest and most popular games from scratch, or brush up on what you already know. Learn to castle, promote your pawns or even play a gambit.
Thursday cooking club is very popular! It’s a lot of fun and allows students to roll their sleeves up and make things that they wouldn’t usually be able to make in the food lessons.
Delicious treats such as Rocky Road, Cookie Dough, Pancakes and Candy Apples, using trees from the Akeley orchard have been on the menu recently.
Our lunchtime sewing club gives students the chance to enjoy our dedicated textiles room and suite of sewing machines outside of timetabled lessons. With 1-to-1 guidance and tuition, students are able to build confidence when using the machines and learn a range of new sewing techniques such as hems, seams, button holes and zips.
They'll be introduced to a range of fabrics and get to practice their new found skills through creating their very own sewn projects.
To view our full Senior Extra-Curricular timetable, get in touch via the enquiry form below:
At Akeley Wood School, our students flourish into individuals that are full of character and potential. Exciting trips happen all year round, to ensure our young individuals are provided with ample opportunity to explore, get creative and most of all have fun! Whether it's a geography trip to France, or a historical visit to an art and archaeology museum, the range of residential trips and days out for students across the school are endless.
Senior School students enjoy residential trips within the UK and around the world, consolidating learning across a wide range of subjects. Our sports tours are extremely popular and, in the past, have included fixture-filled trips to Dubai, Holland and Spain for our budding sports enthusiasts to enjoy. Other trips have included GCSE Geography excursions to Snowdonia National Park, an action-packed adventure across the channel to be immersed in the rich history and language of France.
Next Steps
Akeley Wood School

Careers at Akeley Wood School
Work with us
Akeley Wood School is a dynamic and friendly place to work with opportunities for professional development. We educate around 800 children and have a progressive approach to teaching and learning. We look to recruit high calibre staff committed to achieving the highest standards and to actively take part in the school life. An energetic, flexible and empathic attitude is required with a strong belief that every child can acquire strategies to ensure they fulfil their true potential. Personal integrity, honesty, energy, stamina and enthusiasm are all essential attributes. To view and apply for our current vacancies please visit the Blenheim Schools Careers site below:

pageCache.text:
Inspection Reports
Our Inspection History.
Each of our school stages are inspected by ISI (Independent Schools Inspectorate) on an individual basis. Please find the schools’ most recent inspection reports below. Follow the link to the Independent School Standard Regulations – used by independent schools as a basis for their professional standards – to see the criteria on which a school will be judged for an inspection.
Nursery: Ofsted Report 2019
“Children arrive at the nursery eager to engage in play and learning.” “Children are confident and are keen to learn. They are developing the necessary skills required to support them for the next stages in their learning.”
Nursery: School Inspection Service, April 2016
The Nursery report commends the activities we provide as “supporting continuous improvement,” with children’s social and language skills described as “outstanding.”
Junior School: ISI School Inspection Report 2023
In December 2023 Akeley Wood Junior School was inspected by the Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI).
Akeley Wood Junior School was judged to successfully meet the standards in relation to: - Quality of leadership, management and governance - Quality of education, training and recreation - Quality pupils' physical, mental health and emotional wellbeing - Quality of pupils' social and economic education and contribution to society - Safeguarding
Junior School: ISI Regulatory Compliance Inspection Report 2019
In June 2019 Akeley Wood Junior School was inspected by the Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI) for Regulatory Compliance:
“The school meets the standards in the schedule to the Education (Independent School Standards) Regulations 2014 and relevant requirements of the statutory framework for the Early Years Foundation Stage, and associated requirements, and no further action is required as a result of this inspection.”
Akeley Wood Junior School was judged to successfully meet the standards in relation to: - Quality of education provided - Spiritual, moral, social and cultural development of pupils - Welfare, health and safety of pupils - Suitability of staff, supply staff and proprietors. - Premises of and accommodation at schools - Provision of information - Manner in which complaints are handled - Quality of leadership in and management of school
Junior School: School Inspection Service, April 2016
We are delighted that the School report describes our pupils as “well-rounded individuals who are keen to learn” and notes they are “happy, courteous and friendly.”

pageCache.pageTitle: A Level Results - Akeley Wood School
pageCache.text:
A-Level Results
Our all-encompassing Future Ready program and A-Level curriculum ensure that students are ready for university, degree apprenticeships or first steps into their chosen career and have the academic results, confidence and strength of character needed for their next adventure beyond Akeley. View the latest A-Level results and university destinations.
We are incredibly proud of all our AW6 graduates who have worked tirelessly to achieve tremendous results in their A Levels this year. Each student’s journey at Akeley Wood has been unique, and their success stories are a testament to their dedication, talents and the supportive, values-led environment we strive to create. 2026 Highlights include: 100% A*-B - Computer Science, Fine Art, DT and Music Technology 100% A*- C - Geography and History In an age where we are told that the learning of modern foreign languages is on the decline it is also wonderful to report 100% A*- B grades achieved in French, Spanish and Russian. Maths students also achieved an impressive 71% A*/A with many going on to read mathematically related degrees at university.
Student Highlights
Two of the top achievers of 2026, were friends Naomi and Jake, who both secured their first choice Universities for their future studies. Naomi achieved A*AA, and is off to study Microbiology at the University of Leeds, and Jake, who achieved A*A*A, is looking forward to taking a Gap Year, before studying Geography at Lancaster University. Other students are taking equally exciting routes, from awaiting confirmation on sought-after apprenticeships to embarking on a wide range of degrees at universities across the country.
Next destinations.

pageCache.pageTitle: Sport & Competition - Akeley Wood Junior School
pageCache.text:
Sport & Competition
At Akeley Wood Junior School sport is a key area of school life, where inclusive participation is nurtured and encouraged. Starting with our nursery children PE and games are timetabled into the school week with sessions led by our dedicated sports staff, ensuring that all our children enjoy the benefits of physical education regardless of ability. Sports sessions focus on teamwork, communication and developing skills in a variety of different sports including rugby, hockey, netball, football, tennis, cricket and athletics. Major sports are all offered, and all children from Reception to Year 6 will take weekly swimming lessons in the nearby Wolverton Pool for two terms each year. We wholeheartedly encourage and support those students who are members of local sports clubs and follow their passions in their many varied activities outside of school.
Coaching
Sporting Facilities
Scholarships
Competition
Local Clubs
Exceptional coaching.
Our long-standing Director of Sport, Michael Lemon, and the Head of Girls’ Games, Rhiannon Chapman, have 24 years of service in sport at the Junior School between them, and lead a highly professional Sports Team ensuring that there is a place for all children, regardless of the level they participate at. This means that every student from Year 3 through to Year 6 will have the opportunity to wear the Akeley colours and represent the school competitively. The cross-over between girls and boys sport is also carefully considered.
Our wide-reaching grounds with many grass rugby/football pitches, cricket nets, an all-weather AstroTurf and large Sports Hall mean that sport continues whatever the weather. Our annual Sports Days are a fantastic occasion for our supportive parent community to see their children in action. Our Sixth Form Sports Leaders frequently come down to the Junior School to support the Sports Team at events and festivals, to referee and lead teams of the younger children.
At Akeley we take great pride in showing the continuous development throughout all year groups and in turn seeing pupils flourish and reach their full potential once they reach Year 6.
We offer Sports Scholarships to children who show exceptional talent in their sport in Year 6, to take them through to the Senior School.
On a competitive level, Akeley Junior School is a strong contender.
Long-standing links with local schools means there is a full fixture list in our own and neighbouring counties. Membership of the ISA gives opportunities to compete at a regional and national level, and to host events that see schools come to our setting from far and wide to compete. We have great success this year at the ISA National Athletics Finals. Almost 150 pupils take part in after school sports clubs weekly, and these include activities such as yoga, handball, basketball and badminton as well as the major sports. We offer Sports Scholarships to children who show exceptional talent in their sport in Year 6, to take them through to the Senior School.
Local Sporting Clubs
Our links with local clubs and primary schools continue to strengthen, enabling students to experience sport outside the school gates and at club level. We have relationships with Buckingham Rugby and Hockey Clubs, Whittlebury Golf Club, Stony Stratford Cricket Club, Wolverton Swimming, The MK Netters and Tennis Works from Milton Keynes. This year we have been able to invite local schools to Akeley to experience fixtures in netball, football and cricket. We offer trips to events such as Wimbledon and the MK Dons Stadium for our students. In Half Terms, sport continues as the PE Team deliver different coaching courses alongside SuperCamps . We wholeheartedly encourage and support those students who are members of local sports clubs and follow their passions in their many varied activities outside of school.
Next Steps
Akeley Wood School

pageCache.pageTitle: Sixth Form Curriculum, AW6 - Akeley Wood School
pageCache.text:
AW6 Sixth Form Curriculum
At our Sixth Form, AW6...
We focus on bridging the gap between school and university and prepare students for the excitement and challenge of life beyond study. This is an education for game changers, the studious, disrupters, creative thinkers and leaders in waiting, and is as unique as its students. We believe our approach offers a unique and exceptional Sixth Form education and experience; academic excellence is delivered by a dedicated team of teaching professionals who consistently support students to achieve their best. This is matched by an equally impressive co-curricular and Future Ready Programme. Our offer considers what is required in a workforce of the future, and supports the development of curious, resilient and adaptable young people.
Assessments.
At AW6 we use CAT4 Assessments which produce a rounded profile of the whole child, revealing hidden potential and identifying different learning styles to ensure students reach their full potential. Our teaching professionals deliver an exceptional academic offer. Along with a broad A Level curriculum, we also offer the Extended Project Qualification, English Speaking Board Qualification as well as encouraging our students to engage with a variety of MOOCs (Massive Open Online Courses). This wealth of opportunity enables our students to choose subjects which they both enjoy and can find success in.
A range of subjects.
An Enhanced Curriculum
Art
Business BTEC
Chemistry
Computer Science
Design Technology
Economics
English Literature
EPQ/Cyber EPQ
Geography
Mathematics and Further Mathematics
Media Studies BTEC
Modern Foreign Languages
Music
Music Technology
Psychology
Textiles Art
Physical Education BTEC
Ready for the future.
Our broad A Level curriculum is enhanced with an innovative Future Ready programme, designed to complement every student’s timetable while equipping them with skills that will set them apart in whatever pathway they choose beyond AW6. Alongside their lessons, students will have the opportunity to take part in sessions on debate and public speaking, networking breakfasts as well as national initiatives such as Young Enterprise. Students will also benefit from links with local universities, such as Buckingham University, where visiting lecturers host workshops, give mock interviews and provide excellent advice for anyone considering Higher Education. With an in-house Careers and Futures Lead, all students will receive 1:1 careers advice to help craft their perfect future.
Next Steps
Akeley Wood School

Enriched Curriculum
Enriching the Mind and Body.
We're proud of our Academic Curriculum, designed to get the best from every child and push them to be as successful as they can. We're equally proud of our distinct Friday afternoons at Akeley Wood Senior School, entirely dedicated to our Enriched Curriculum programme. This programme is additional to the fantastic extra-curricular offer of Sport, Music and Creative Arts that is timetabled into the week and provided within extra lunchtime and after school clubs at Akeley.
Akeley Friday Afternoons.
On Friday afternoons, each student chooses an activity to stimulate their body and mind, and we actively encourage them to try something new. The clubs, offered on a termly rotation, are varied in discipline and scope and there is something for everyone here. Students of all ages, across the Senior School, mix in these activities. We think this adds to community cohesion across the school, encouraging pupils to mentor and support each other, especially in the context of discovering something new. We also offer Sixth Form students the opportunity to assist in running the sessions.
A variety of unique and enriching clubs, with something for everyone.
This group meets to discuss and act upon environmental issue both locally and globally. If you care about looking after our planet and want to take action alongside like-minded souls - then this is the club for you.
This group meets weekly to improve fitness and enjoy the stunning countryside we are lucky to have surrounding our school. We encourage walking and running and most importantly each other!
Create a range of games including Pong, Snake, Space Invaders, Falling Skies, Missile Command and Maze. Develop your own games working individually or in small groups using self-help guides and videos, or come up with your own original concept and design!
Come and develop your confidence with public speaking and engage in interesting topics with Akeley's very own debating club. There's a new topic each week to develop your skills with engaging debating games and techniques.
Shooting technique, the layout of the Archery range and equipment maintenance is all covered in this activity. You can try and improve on your PB week by week and take part in competitions to win prizes.
Students travel to the nearby Swan Pool in Buckingham where they are taught the main strokes of front crawl, backstroke, breaststroke and butterfly and spend time each week refining their skills. They will also master tumble turns, and learn life-saving drills. This is a very popular Friday afternoon activity.
Our younger students also get to enjoy a myriad of activities beyond the classroom and academic curriculum. Explore the fantastic extra-curricular programme on offer at Akeley Wood Junior School and discover how children from Reception to Year 6 are also encouraged to expand their horizons and try something new.
Next Steps
Akeley Wood School

pageCache.pageTitle: Extra Curricular Activities & Clubs - Akeley Wood School
pageCache.text:
Extra Curricular Activities
Together, our students, parents and teaching staff make up a vibrant community of individuals at Akeley Wood with a shared passion that teaching and learning should not be confined to the classroom. We strive to harness the creative spirit of our students and encourage self-expression from a very young age, giving our students every opportunity to discover what they love and have the courage to try many new things during their time at school.
Something for everyone
Our fun and inventive extra-curricular programme is a key part of informal learning and a great opportunity to make new friends and to build social confidence, resourcefulness and problem-solving skills. From Reception upwards, children can participate in around 35 different activities crafted to reinforce teaching in the curriculum, as well as supporting existing passions and nurturing new ones. Extra-curricular activities take place during break and lunch times or after school. Most students will get involved in several activities across the week and they range enormously in scope. Whether it be gardening or chess, programming, sports, yoga or band practice, there is something for all tastes and talents.
Wrap around care
Trips & Residentials
Junior
Our wrap around care sessions provide the perfect solution for parents needing to drop off and pick up their children outside the normal school times. Our before and after school sessions are available at a small fee and can be booked via our Parent Pay app, Blenheim Connect. Early Drop off starts at 8am. Akeley After School Club is from 4.00pm – 6.00pm and includes an afternoon tea followed by time to complete home learning and participate in fun after school activities.
Senior
Students can be dropped off from 8.00am at our Senior school site ready for the start of the day at 8.30am. For those needing to pick up their child later than the normal school pick up times, there are after school clubs every day of the week along with a homework club from Monday – Thursday. This finishes at 5.30pm and is provided at no extra cost.
Trips & Residentials
Junior Trips
Whether it's a sports trip to Big Rock climbing centre or a historical visit to an art and archaeology museum, the range of residential trips and days out for students across the school are endless. From Year 3 our Junior school students take part in annual residential trips, which vary from epic adventures at Land and Wave in Dorset, to glamping in the forest at Camp Wilderness in Hertfordshire, leaving children with a fantastic set of memories alongside new-found confidence.
Senior Trips
Senior School students enjoy residential trips within the UK and around the world, consolidating learning across a wide range of subjects. Our sports tours are extremely popular and include fixture-filled trips to Dubai, Holland and Spain for all of our budding sports enthusiasts to enjoy. Other trips have included GCSE Geography excursions to Snowdonia National Park, an action packed adventure across the channel to be immersed in and surrounded by the history and language of France, as well as a Performing Arts and Music trip across the pond to the Big Apple itself!
Next Steps
Akeley Wood School

pageCache.pageTitle: Junior School Curriculum - Akeley Wood School
pageCache.text:
Junior School Curriculum
We are proud of our exciting and varied curriculum at Akeley Wood Junior School. It is under constant scrutiny and review to ensure it provides focus on the development of knowledge and skills in a fun, interactive and responsible way. We encourage active participation and aim to provide a curriculum to develop children with a love of learning. We aim to create an environment in both taught lessons and beyond, where academic risk-taking, questioning and debating, challenging thinking and the freedom to learn from mistakes are all accepted and encouraged.
Academic Curriculum
Our taught curriculum broadly follows the EYFS framework for Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) and the English National Curriculum for Key Stage 1 (KS1) and Key Stage 2 (KS2). Teachers plan lessons to support children to achieve age related End of Year Expectations for their year group. Our pupils take GL Summative Assessments at the end of Years 1-6 in English and Mathematics. Our curriculum is inclusive. For those pupils with special educational needs, the school uses well established Learning Support programmes led by the SENCo and Inclusion Lead. We also have an Exceptional Potential Programme, ensuring those children exceeding expectations are challenged appropriately.
Children at Akeley have access to a variety of specialist teaching throughout the school year.
Our specialist teachers in PE, Music, Art, Modern Foreign Languages (MFL), Forest School, Design Technology, Cooking and Nutrition and Computer Science plan a broad and varied curriculum, giving students an excellent understanding of specific subject areas alongside their core subjects.
A wide range of enrichment and extra-curricular activities supplement the timetabled curriculum. Our pupils are encouraged to take part in an extensive range of Art, Drama, Music, Sport and many more activities and clubs.
We focus on themed days and weeks to enrich learning. Pupils are also taken to places of interest on a regular basis. Visits, including residential opportunities, are organised annually to help develop independence, teamwork and responsibility in an environment outside the school gates.
PSHE (Personal, Social, Health and Economic) Education is a school curriculum subject through which pupils develop the knowledge, skills and attributes they need to manage their lives, now and in the future.
PSHE lessons help pupils to stay healthy, safe and prepared for life – and work – in modern Britain. When taught well, PSHE also helps pupils to achieve their academic potential.
CENTURY Tech combines artificial intelligence with the latest research in learning science and neuroscience. This online platform will further enhance learning for all students, in either English or Mathematics, by identifying strengths, gaps in knowledge and misconceptions.
A personalised pathway is determined for each child and is reviewed regularly by the child’s class teacher, as well as leaders of English and Maths.
Next Steps
Akeley Wood School

pageCache.pageTitle: Extra-Curricular Activities & Clubs - Akeley Wood Junior School
pageCache.text:
Extra-Curricular Activities
Our extra-curricular offering at the Junior School is dazzling! We offer a combination of lunchtime and after-school clubs run by our teachers, and others run by external providers that come to Wicken Park to run sessions with the children each week. The clubs include many subjects taken across the week as part of our curriculum such as Music, Times Tables Rockstars and Art, but allow children extra time to explore the subject more fully. There are also many more clubs where children can try something entirely new, such as Young Farmers Club, where children work on crafts and are able to sell them from time to time on a stall at school to parents and visitors.
We also offer sessions in Yoga, Programming, Girls’ Tag Rugby, Cooking, Creative Writing, Music Tech, Lacrosse, Street Dance and Watercolour painting. Whatever your child is into, we have something to inspire their passion, creativity and sense of fun! We believe extra-curricular education has a key role to play in the development of the whole child academically, socially and emotionally.
This club gives budding authors the opportunity to unleash their imagination and create their own stories with encouragement and guidance. At Creative Writing club children can explore different creative writing techniques and create their own fantastic fictional characters.
At Cooking Club children will learn about food preparation and different ingredients in our well-equipped Cooking and Nutrition Kitchen, while making some delicious dishes and having lots of fun with their friends. A definite skill for life – you can never start too early!
Music Technology club gives the children a unique opportunity to make exciting music through a series of fun and engaging projects, using music sequencing software. In this session, your children can enhance their creativity and individual expression through the power of music!
This is a really energetic club, perfect for blowing off some steam after the school day! Children will learn to outwit their opponents while honing their hand-eye coordination and learning lots of skills such as throwing, dodging and footwork.
After-school extra-curricular clubs run from 3.45-4.30pm
Junior trips.
Our Junior School children enjoy a plethora of trips, designed to extend our student's educational experience, build independence and to provide memorable experiences beyond the classroom. Day trips are offered to children in every year group and are always looked forward to with much anticipation; from visits to Big Rock climbing centre, Woburn Safari Park and the Ashmolean Museum of Art and Archaeology. Residential trips are offered from Year 3 upwards and vary from epic adventures at Land and Wave in Dorset, to glamping in the forest at Camp Wilderness in Hertfordshire, leaving children with a fantastic set of memories alongside new found confidence.
Next Steps
Akeley Wood School

pageCache.pageTitle: Private Senior School In Buckinghamshire - Akeley Wood School
pageCache.text:
Senior School
Welcome to Akeley Wood Senior School.
We are an inclusive, family orientated school, offering incredible experiences both inside and outside of the classroom. We believe in encouraging pupils to seize opportunities from the broad range of subjects and activities on offer, through our strong academic offer and extensive extra-curricular opportunities. Akeley’s vibrant and engaging community is located across three stunning campuses, all located between Buckingham and Stony Stratford. Wicken Park is home to our Nursery to Year 6 children, at Akeley Wood House we educate our Senior School students aged 11 to 16, and our Sixth Form, ‘AW6’, is located along the same road as the Senior School, at the impressive Tile House Mansion.
On each campus, we have created a learning environment where children feel comfortable to grow, but are also challenged to think and act independently. The teaching and support teams at the school are dedicated to making the educational experience here the best it can be. They challenge, they inspire, they have high expectations and most of all, they care.
Developing soft skills is one of the key strengths of an Akeley education. When students leave us at 18, they enter a world that can be challenging and complex. Our role is to help to build character and resilience that enables them to face the world beyond the school gates with confidence and a ‘can do’ attitude. We are also keen to equip them with a set of examination results of which they can be rightly proud. At Akeley, every child is encouraged to ‘Be You. Brilliantly.’
Academic excellence.
Deliberately small class sizes ensure our teachers give each child the time and attention they need to develop at their own pace, immerse themselves in what they enjoy and reach their full potential academically. Students are assessed regularly to ensure that they are given the framework and support they need as an individual, enabling them to go on to achieve great things.
Enriched curriculum.
Our Friday afternoon Enriched Curriculum programme is steered towards consolidating and enhancing the timetabled curriculum, with fun and stimulating activities in an informal setting. This offers an opportunity to try something completely new and for year groups to mix. Each term students get to choose from a variety of different activites, from snowboarding to special effects makeup!
Beyond the classroom.
At Akeley, we believe in developing well-rounded students who have the room to discover new talents while benefiting from contextual and applied education, in and out of the classroom. Thanks to a brilliant extra-curricular programme, a multitude of trips and residentials, as well as fantastic Outdoor Learning facilities, our students constantly benefit from experiential learning across the curriculum.
Akeley Wood House
Akeley Wood Senior School combines historic grandeur with state-of-the-art facilities. The buildings have been adapted and equipped for modern, 21st century education and offer the ideal environment in which big ideas can flourish, inspiring a lifelong passion for discovery in all our students.
Begin your Akeley Wood School journey.
Straightforward and simple

pageCache.pageTitle: Senior School Facilities & Location - Akeley Wood School
pageCache.text:
Senior School and AW6 Facilities
Contemporary facilities in a beautifully historic setting.
Our Senior School and Sixth Form campus combines beautiful historic buildings with purpose-built contemporary facilities, artfully constructed to maintain the character of the stunning site. Our fully-equipped teaching areas include classrooms, laboratories, specialist rooms for art, textiles, design technology, music, film studies, food and nutrition, drama, and a spectacular Outdoor Learning area, deep in the woods. This provides a stimulating and engaging environment for teaching and learning in which students thrive. Our provision of excellent sports facilities reflects the prominence of PE, sport and games at Akeley Wood. Our sports dome, provides sheltered multi-use facilities, and sits alongside our many rugby/football pitches, netball courts, astro-turf pitches and tennis courts where many a school sporting record is set.
Facilities at-a-glance:
Outdoor Learning area, complete with low ropes course, fire-pit, axe throwing and space for den building
Specialist classrooms including a music technology suite, a newly refurbished design technology workshop and drama studio.
Vast sporting facilities including a multi-use sports dome, astro-turf, rugby pitches and cricket nets
Onsite orchard, regularly used to supply fruit for Food and Nutrition lessons
Why not come and visit?
We believe that the best way for you to understand the quality of our facilities is to visit us for an Open Morning or Breakfast with the Head event. Here you’ll get a chance to see what we have to offer your child and get a feel for the ethos of the school.
Purpose-built learning spaces.

pageCache.pageTitle: AW6 Future Ready - Akeley Wood School
pageCache.text:
AW6: Future Ready
At AW6 we focus on preparing our students for the future to ensure they are ready for anything at the end of their two years with us. We have a strong team of teaching and pastoral staff at AW6, including Mark Lambert, our University, Careers and Futures Lead. This ensures students have continued access to a qualified Careers Adviser for expert advice and more informal interactions. He leads our innovative and multi-layered Future Ready programme, that is built upon several key elements.
The AW6 Enrichment Experience
Young Enterprise
Next Destinations
Networking.
Students are armed with the confidence and tools needed to form contacts and build professional relationships beyond the classroom. They are encouraged to attend the frequent networking events held at AW6 across the year, including breakfast meetups, with a range of professionals from across industry. Our University, Careers and Futures Lead holds sessions on the why and how of networking and our students have many opportunities for business visits, and events such as LawFest with the University of Buckingham.
University and Workplace links
We want all our students to have aspirations and to achieve their goals whatever they may be. Our strong link with The University of Buckingham means a regular presence at AW6 to offer students support from mock university interviews to workshops and discussions on university life. Our programme of Wednesday Webinars allow students to find out online about a range of universities both in the UK and abroad. Many of our students will follow alternative pathways such as workplace internships, degree apprenticeships or go straight into the world of work. Our expert team will support young people in whatever they need, be it UCAS applications, Oxbridge, BMAT, degree apprenticeship programmes and career options. Whatever their future, we want students to make good and informed decisions about their next step.
The AW6 Enrichment Experience
Students get so much out of their time at AW6 beyond the classroom. Our calendar is packed full of trips, events and initiatives designed to develop character and ensure every opportunity for our young people to become socially and globally aware citizens of the world.
We organise industry visits and days out to university and careers shows. Our Leadership-focussed trip to the Active Learning Group centre at Cuffley is popular, and our departments organise many curriculum-linked trips. We aim to make sure that the world outside AW6 is fully visible to our students. Our AW6 Student Leadership Teams sit on committees based on our school values to initiate activities linked to the environment, community values, wellbeing and diversity and inclusion. Recent events include a fundraising event for Ukraine featuring a set by our AW6 bands, and a sleepout to support the local branch of the YMCA. Our Future Ready Enrichment curriculum takes place across the week, where students can get involved in diverse activities such as debating at Verbal Fight Club, being trained as a mentor, participating in sport or engaging in academic enrichment beyond the A Level subject curriculum.
Young Enterprise
This national competition gives students the opportunity to be part of a real business made up of a team of their Sixth Form peers. Young Enterprise equips participants with the skills for the workplace and gives them hands-on experience of running a business which will sink or swim depending on the team’s competence and drive. Each year we have a team of students who get involved with this fantastic project, supported by our AW6 teaching team and external guest experts.
EPQ
An EPQ is an A level standard qualification designed to extend and stretch a student’s abilities beyond the A Level curriculum. Focussing on a topic of their choice, this in-depth investigation is an effective way to work on project management skills and is an invaluable addition to any Higher Education or job application beyond AW6.
Unifrog
At AW6 we use Unifrog to great effect, and it is very popular with our students. It is a nationally recognised career platform that brings all available information all together into one single location for students to make the best choices and submit the strongest applications to their next step. The platform includes UCAS applications as well as apprenticeships and Further Education Colleges and has a section where students can find helpful tips on CV writing, interviews and common application questions. The platform enables teachers, parents and mentors to keep up to date with an applicant’s progress.
Next Destinations
We are incredibly proud of the sheer variety and breadth of courses, institutions and careers that our students go on to after their time at AW6. We are very definitely not a ‘one size fits all’ establishment, and this range of destinations proves that our tailored combination of academic rigour, comprehensive Future-Ready support and pastoral care allows every student to find their own passion and follow their own path, whatever that may be.
